## Recommendation

- **Go to St. Joseph's pier, rated 1 (below average).** It's the only one of the four with a recent pier mention of salmon, though that report is from Aug 24 and the method was unclear.
- **South Haven: 1, but I have no pier data for it.** Boats did well there last week, but that doesn't tell you about the pier.
- **Grand Haven: 1.** The latest pier report there was slow.
- **Muskegon: 0.** The latest report said no salmon were reported from the breakwalls.
- **Expect slow pier fishing everywhere.** If you want a better bite, the boat reports were the strongest recent salmon news. Check conditions before you go, since the pier reports are a week old.

## Why

- Pier fishing was slow at the most recent reports: Grand Haven was "slow for salmon" and Muskegon had "no salmon … from the breakwalls" (Grand Haven and Muskegon, 2022-09-07).
- St. Joseph is the only port with a recent pier mention of fish: "a few fish around the piers," from a report that didn't say whether the anglers were on a pier (St. Joseph, 2022-08-24).
- I'd expect the pier to stay slow for now, because past reports at similar water temperatures (about 72 F) also described slow pier fishing (similar past weeks, Grand Haven and Muskegon).

## Evidence

**Recent reports (latest is 2022-09-07, six days old)**
- Grand Haven, 2022-09-07, pier: quality 0 (slow), "The pier action was slow for salmon." Boats: quality 2, 40–120 ft of water, fish 40–85 ft down on glow spoons and green or white flies.
- Muskegon, 2022-09-07, pier: quality 0, "No salmon were reported from the breakwalls." Boats: quality 2, fish 45–90 ft down in 60–120 ft of water.
- South Haven, 2022-09-07: no pier report. Boats: quality 3 (good), "Salmon anglers reported pretty good fishing this week," mostly in 110–120 ft of water, with the best water around 40 ft.
- St. Joseph, 2022-09-07: no pier report. Boats: quality 1, "The best water was around 100 feet."
- St. Joseph, 2022-08-24: "There seemed to be a few fish around the piers," quality 1, but the method was not stated.
- Piers were closed at South Haven for several days in early August because of red flags (South Haven, 2022-08-10). This is not a current closure.

**Past seasons (similar weeks, surface water about 72 F)**
- The similar past weeks match the recent reports closely. Pier action was slow at Grand Haven and Muskegon (2022-09-07, same weeks). I didn't find any pier-specific salmon report at South Haven in that window.

**Conditions now (the week before 2022-09-13; the tool was in backtest mode, so these are not live readings)**
- Buoy surface water was about 72–73 F, falling 1 F over the week at every port. The near-pier satellite reading (GLSEA) was 71–72 F and falling 1 F in the last three days at all four ports.
- Upwelling-favorable wind (north to east, 8+ mph) totaled 35 h at South Haven and 40 h at Muskegon over the week, but only 6 h at St. Joseph. In the last three days it was 16 h at South Haven, 14 h at Muskegon, 4 h at Grand Haven and 6 h at St. Joseph.

## Caveats

- The newest report is from 2022-09-07, six days old. Conditions can change quickly in the fall, and the conditions shown are the week before 2022-09-13, not live readings.
- The pier ratings are my judgment from weak evidence. South Haven and St. Joseph have no recent pier-specific salmon report, so their 1s are guesses from thin data.
- General guidance (Michigan Sea Grant): upwelling brings cold water and salmon toward piers. Upwelling-favorable wind was higher at South Haven and Muskegon than at St. Joseph last week, but none of the pier reports confirmed it; I'd expect a fresh north or east wind to help the pier bite, but that is my inference, not a report.
- Water near 72 F is warm for Chinook (general guidance from NY DEC: 52–58 F). Salmon are likely deeper than the pier can reach, which fits the boat reports.
